description: Farm Mechanics covers the machines that keep farms running: shop safety and warning symbols, how engines, hydraulics and transmissions deliver power, tool care, maintaining equipment, and careers in farm mechanics.

safety.note: Farm machinery is dangerous: work only with an experienced adult, with engines off and parts secured.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Requirements 5 and 6 were not visible in the excerpts and are not outlined yet.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Safety
requirements.summary: Safety equipment and clothing, a farm-shop plan, warning symbols and safety data sheets.

requirements.title: Power
requirements.summary: How power is produced or transferred in a diesel engine, a hydraulic system and a transmission.

requirements.title: Tool work
requirements.summary: Two tool tasks, such as replacing a handle or dressing a chisel or screwdriver tip.

requirements.title: Machine maintenance
requirements.summary: One option, such as servicing a machine, a preoperation checklist or winter storage.

requirements.title: Careers
requirements.summary: Careers in farm mechanics and the education one of them requires.
